prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent bumped CTS sink-cluster diameter/size, which made the clock tree worse. Revert that and instead disable CTS sink clustering entirely (cluster_size 1 / diameter small) so CTS builds a balanced H-tree with per-sink buffering; this reduces long clock detours and buffer-induced congestion, lowering propagated-clock WNS/TNS without increasing overflow.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.044 robust(mean-std)=-0.019 min_case=-0.023 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=-0.023 dWNS=+6.8% dTNS=-8.8% overflow~123
  bp-ng45: score=+0.059 dWNS=+10.2% dTNS=+3.0% overflow~124
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.008 dWNS=-7.0% dTNS=+5.8% overflow~76
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Mixed: hypothesis only partly holds. Ariane133-ng45 improves TNS (-8.8%) but WNS worsens (+6.8%), and bp_fe-ng45 WNS degrades (+7.0%) despite TNS gain—suggesting disabling clustering helps some sinks but hurts critical paths, plausibly from added per-sink buffering/detour on tight paths. bp-ng45 improves both. Robust score is negative (-0.019), so the change is not a clear win. Next step: apply clustering disable selectively (e.g., only non-critical sink groups or cap cluster diameter) and re-run to isolate the WNS regression on ariane/bp_fe.
